reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a Binance crypto arbitrage opportunity with claimed monthly earnings and high daily or unlimited earnings language. It directs viewers to register and verify through a link and ties participation to crypto and fiat transfers, a 100 USDT minimum sale, NGN deposits, and account details for funding. the available video evidence does not establish completed losses, guaranteed outcomes, or the trustworthiness of any specific counterparty.

citations.quote: BINANCE ARBITRAGE: make #100000 per month beginner guide
there are several ways to trade in this same place
before you can sell you have to have a minimum of a hundred USDT on your account
I can either buy from someone directly here or sell
if I'm going to transfer this BTC to this guy this guy is going to give me 12.31 dollars

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present buying and selling as automatic profit. His own worked example says the buyer would lose about 600, and he warns viewers to check a counterparty's completion rate before placing an order. He also points out that a merchant fee increased while he was demonstrating it. Those cautions matter when assessing the earnings language in the title: the spoken instruction exposes unfavorable pricing, counterparty risk, and changing costs rather than concealing them behind a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: in this case right now is it you are losing about six hundred
if you are going to order from here you have to look at the completion rates
here at the fee you can see that here it has increased to 150 before now it was 100 nera
BINANCE ARBITRAGE: make #100000 per month beginner guide

rebuttal.rebuttal: The monthly earnings headline deserves scrutiny, but the opening treats the 100 USDT statement as a condition for participation in a profitable scheme. The speaker describes it as a minimum before selling, then explicitly shows a buy-and-sell example that loses money. Nor does his description of a BTC transfer establish that the viewer will earn a return from making one. These details weaken the inference that the walkthrough promises profitable arbitrage.

citations.quote: before you can sell you have to have a minimum of a hundred USDT on your account
in this case right now is it you are losing about six hundred
if I'm going to transfer this BTC to this guy this guy is going to give me 12.31 dollars

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A losing example and cautions about fees do not erase the video's invitation to earn through Binance arbitrage. The title makes a specific monthly earnings claim, while the speaker says he will introduce ways to earn and offers a registration link to viewers without verified accounts. The risks he mentions may qualify individual transactions, but they do not account for the prominent income pitch.

citations.quote: BINANCE ARBITRAGE: make #100000 per month beginner guide
I'll be introducing you to binance and their several ways to also earn as well on binance
if you don't have a verified account I will drop a link where from there you can register and verify account

opening.argument: Judge, follow the actual lesson rather than treating its headline as the whole video. The speaker navigates a verified Binance account, compares a proposed BTC purchase with the amount obtainable on resale, then walks through P2P limits, buying by card, and depositing NGN. He even says he cannot complete the example sale because he did not buy the BTC, and says his account is not funded for launching an ad. That is a screen-based operational demonstration with hypothetical amounts and incomplete transactions, not evidence that he took viewers' funds or delivered the advertised monthly earnings.

you can see that the same insufficient amount because i didn't really buy it
i need a minimum of 100 usdt which as for now i've not founded my account yet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies the headline, proposed registration link, and transfer steps. But those points occur within an account walkthrough: the speaker explains verification as a condition for reaching P2P and compares buying and selling on the interface. The cited 100 USDT is a stated selling threshold, not proof of a payment to the speaker. The later BTC-for-dollars example describes what a counterparty would pay; it does not establish a completed transaction or a monthly return.

citations.quote: if you are not verified you will not get to this place
before you can sell you have to have a minimum of a hundred USDT on your account
if I'm going to transfer this BTC to this guy this guy is going to give me 12.31 dollars

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial format can still promote a questionable earnings opportunity. Here the title promises a monthly amount from Binance arbitrage, and the speaker frames the account tour as an introduction to ways to earn. He also offers a registration link and explains account funding and transfers. The fact that his example trades are incomplete limits what they prove about outcomes; it does not remove the income claim or the steps inviting viewers into the workflow.

I'm going to transfer it no to my Binance to the merchant account

opening.argument: Judge, the concrete transactions described are purchases, sales, deposits, and payments, not a contract promising returns on money entrusted to the speaker. The registration link is described as a way to open and verify a Binance account. The deposit explanation distinguishes a merchant's fee from Binance's fee, and the closing example describes exchanging BTC for dollars to fund an account or pay online. The record does not show a request to send crypto to the speaker, hand over credentials, recruit others, or buy a bot or funded contract. The title's earnings claim is concerning, but these missing elements matter when deciding what mechanism the video actually presents.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening connects the link, balance threshold, deposits, and transfers to an earnings pitch, but it does not identify a payment requested by the speaker or a promised payout from a bot or contract. The speaker instead describes buying from or selling to people on P2P, and the 100 USDT amount as a prerequisite for selling. Those facts support scrutiny of the headline; they do not by themselves establish the alleged mechanism.

citations.quote: I can either buy from someone directly here or sell
before you can sell you have to have a minimum of a hundred USDT on your account
BINANCE ARBITRAGE: make #100000 per month beginner guide

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a demonstrated bot, contract, or payment to the speaker narrows what can be concluded, but it does not make the video ordinary commerce. The title explicitly advertises monthly earnings through arbitrage, and the description includes daily and unlimited arbitrage earnings language. The speaker then supplies registration, buying, selling, and funding instructions. The concern is that an income pitch is paired with actionable trading steps, not that a loss or a private payment has been proved.
